Variants.Content: Numidian light horsemen from North Africa were celebrated as the finest skirmish cavalry of the ancient world. Riding small, wiry horses without bridles, bits, or saddles—guided solely by a simple halter rope and riding stick—they hurled light javelins with pinpoint accuracy. Masters of feigned retreats and harassing skirmishes, they repeatedly lured rigid Roman formations into devastating ambushes.
